issues.description: The constructor parameter type for PersonResource differs between the template and the solution. The template defines PersonResource(PersonService personService) (allowing proper Spring dependency injection), while the solution defines PersonResource(String personService) which does not match the declared field type (PersonService) and will break constructor-based injection and compilation. This structural mismatch makes the solution unusable and conflicts with the intended design of a service-injected REST controller.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution's PersonResource to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the field (public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). This restores compatibility with the field declaration and enables Spring to inject the service.

issues.description: The conceptual dependency 'PersonService' is referenced inconsistently in PersonResource: the problem statement and the template expect PersonResource to receive a PersonService instance, but the solution's PersonResource constructor accepts a String (parameter named personService). This mismatches the intended dependency identifier/type and will confuse students mapping the 'PersonService' concept to the REST controller (and will also break dependency injection).
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution, change the PersonResource constructor signature to accept PersonService (not String) and assign it to the personService field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This restores a consistent identifier/type mapping with the problem statement and template.
